note: Authoritative local data from L1 chains.db (DeFiLlama + CoinGecko + growthepie/Dune). Raw signals, no scores. null = NO DATA (do not guess). FRESHNESS: price & market caps are live (today); TVL/stablecoin LEVELS are the latest available (carried forward if a chain's today-point isn't in yet); daily-FLOW metrics (DEX volume, fees, active_addresses, tx_count) are the LAST COMPLETE UTC DAY (today is partial and excluded) — full-day figures, use them as-is. SHARES are each chain's % of the WHOLE DeFi market (all ~500 chains; denominators in market.total_*), so tracked chains sum to <100% and deltas are immune to which chains we track. TVL/volume are USD-denominated, so share moves in a big market swing partly reflect token price, not pure flows. Each chain ALSO carries its OWN raw TVL growth — tvl_change_1d/7d/30d_pct (chain's level vs itself N days ago); use THESE for 'is this chain's TVL growing', NOT the share deltas (share = slice of market, a different question). If tvl_suspect_1d is true the 1d move is a likely upstream data glitch (a >25% one-day swing) — discount the 1d figure and lean on the 7d/30d trend instead. Stablecoins mirror this: stable_change_1d/7d/30d_pct are the chain's OWN stablecoin-supply trend (use for 'is stablecoin capital arriving/leaving', and to confirm or debunk 'stables doubled/halved' claims); stable_suspect_1d flags a >30% one-day swing as a likely DeFiLlama adapter flap (a bridged asset dropping in/out of the index) — call it out as a data-quality event, not a capital flow, and lean on 7d/30d. N-days-ago baselines are median-smoothed, so a one-day glitch can't fake a 7d/30d trend.

signal_glossary.volume_heat: Volume is large vs market cap (turnover ≥15%) — unusual interest building.
signal_glossary.vol_leads_price: Volume is hot but 7d price hasn't run yet — interest building BEFORE the move (the early sweet spot).
signal_glossary.momentum: 7d gain keeping pace with / exceeding 30d — the move is accelerating, not fading.
signal_glossary.low_float: Only a small share of supply circulates — CAUTION: unlock overhang can cap upside.
signal_glossary.tvl_surge: On-chain TVL jumped ≥25% in 7d from a small base — real capital arriving, not just token price.

pre_winner_lookalikes.method: validated winner-DNA coil screen (deep-below-high + oversold + at-30d-low [all validated, hold OOS] + below-ATH/high-vol/mid-float/small-cap); primed-but-not-yet-moved. NECESSARY-not-sufficient setup — needs an event trigger.
pre_winner_lookalikes.how_to_use: Beaten-down coils matching the data-validated winner DNA. SETUPS, not buys: most never move. Edge comes ONLY from confluence — a lookalike that is also trending / in a heating narrative / has a near catalyst / has fresh dev-gov.

signal_glossary.deep_below_60d_high: Trading <50% of its 60-day high — deeply beaten down. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.oversold_30d: Down >25% over 30 days — oversold. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.at_30d_low: Trading within ~3% of its 30-day low RIGHT NOW — the capitulation launch zone. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample); a bounce off the low actually LOWERS winner odds, so this is a timing edge.
signal_glossary.oversold_90d: Down >40% over 90 days — sustained downtrend (supporting context).
signal_glossary.deep_below_ath: Trading <15% of all-time high — far from prior peak, room to recover.
signal_glossary.high_vol: Elevated 30d volatility — capable of large moves.
signal_glossary.mid_float: Meaningful but not-fully-diluted float — the winner sweet spot.
signal_glossary.small_cap: Sub-$100M market cap — small enough to multiply.

Each item carries release_notes / body (truncated) + a keyword dimension_hint (raw, NOT a verdict) — the FOLLOW-UP is to read these and judge what the change actually does and whether it improves the protocol at a fundamental level (consensus/scaling/security/economics/new capability) vs routine housekeeping. dev.release_notes:
Austin hardfork release for the Polygon PoS Bor execution client.

## Activation

| Network | Block |
| --- | --- |
| Amoy | 44,120,000 |
| Mainnet | 91,949,700 |

## What's Changed
* Release v2.10.0 (Austin hardfork) by @kamuikatsurgi in https://github.com/0xPolygon/bor/pull/2360

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/0xPolygon/bor/compare/v2.9.0...v2.10.0

## Protocol
#### Sui Protocol Version in this release: `133`

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27667: Add some additional bounds and relax some others.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27155: Bumps the max protocol version to 131 and adds the `framework_tx_context_mut_restrictions` feature flag. Starting at version 131, system-package functions that take `&mut TxContext` and return a mutable reference must also take a non-`TxContext` `&mut` parameter; publication is rejected otherwise. User packages are unaffected.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/26891: Adds a `ForwardingAddressRegistry` system object (`0x2::forwarding_address`, object ID `0xfa`), created during epoch change when the `create_forwarding_address_registry` flag is enabled (devnet only for now). No user-facing API yet.

## Nodes (Validators and Full nodes)

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/26891: New end-of-epoch system transaction `ForwardingAddressRegistryCreate`.

## gRPC

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/26891: New `FORWARDING_ADDRESS_REGISTRY_CREATE` kind in the `EndOfEpochTransactionKind` proto enum.

## GraphQL

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/26891: New `ForwardingAddressRegistryCreateTransaction` member of the `EndOfEpochTransactionKind` union.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27492: `transactions(filter: {affectedObject: ...})` now correctly returns a `FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE` error when the `tx_affected_objects` pipeline isn't configured, instead of silently …[truncated]

### **Authors**

Frax Core Team

---

## **Summary**

This proposal seeks to authorize the sfrxUSD strategy framework to allocate up to **1,000,000 frxUSD** into the Royco SLP. The objective is to provide redemption liquidity for sr-srRoyUSDC while earning yield generated by the underlying srRoyUSDC strategy, expanding sfrxUSD's portfolio of governance-approved yield strategies and strengthening frxUSD's role within the Royco ecosystem.

---

## **Background & Motivation**

As sfrxUSD continues to expand its benchmark-rate strategy, the protocol seeks to diversify across governance-approved opportunities that combine attractive risk-adjusted returns with strategic ecosystem growth.

The Royco SLP serves as the primary redemption mechanism for srRoyUSDC and enables users to enter and exit positions through deep onchain liquidity. Supporting this pool allows frxUSD to become a core liquidity asset within the Royco ecosystem while generating yield from the underlying strategy.

This proposal establishes an initial allocation cap for the strategy while allowing the Frax Core Team to deploy capital prudently based on market conditions and ongoing risk assessment.

Frax Core Team

## Summary

This proposal adds the Gearbox Institutional RWA lending market to the sfrxUSD AMO whitelist with a cap of **$5,000,000**.

The market is an frxUSD-denominated lending pool collateralized entirely by regulated tokenized assets from BNY and VanEck (via Securitize) and Fasanara (via Midas). Every borrower is KYCed, all collateral is transfer-restricted at the token level besides mF-ONE, and idle liquidity sits in frxUSD earning T-Bill yield.

---

## Background

Tokenized RWA markets are one of the fastest growing categories as institutions move onchain. The Gearbox RWA markets are a strategic opportunity to position frxUSD at the center of this growth. Two DeFi-native OGs, Frax and Gearbox, bringing best practices of DeFi capital-efficiency to bring the highest risk-adjusted returns to institutions with institutional assets.

Issuer acceptance of frxUSD as a subscription asset is compounding as frxUSD grows.
